newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU agrees law to counter U.S. anti-Cuba moves.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees law to counter U.S. anti-Cuba moves.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers agreed a new law on Monday to counter U.S. anti-Cuba legislation, EU diplomats said.
Agreement came after the proposed law was amended to allow Denmark, which had initially threatened to veto it, to support the measure.
At issue is the Helms-Burton law, a U.S. measure which threatens European companies and individuals with lawsuits if they trade with Cuba.
The EU has bitterly opposed the U.S. law, saying it violates world trading rules by extending its jurisdiction over foreign companies.
The new EU law is a counter-strike, forbidding European companies or individuals from complying with U.S. litigation and also allowing them to counter-sue in Europe.
"Everyone is happy; the Danes have accepted a formula," said another diplomat.
Denmark had opposed the EU law on the grounds that it was based on legal provisions that compromised national sovereignty.
EU legal experts spent most of the day on Monday looking for ways to amend the proposed law to give it the same effect but without using the provisions opposed by Denmark.

Until Denmark raised its legal objections last week, the EU had seen its unanimous opposition to the Washington law as a rare example of the 15-nation bloc being able to speak with one voice on a foreign policy matter.
